name: DaVinci Timeline Shortcuts Efficiency
use_when: A Resolve short-form workflow needs faster cutting, duplicating, moving, and Fusion access.
The editor is repeatedly doing slow manual timeline operations.
A high-volume shorts workflow needs consistent speed.
A full Resolve edit needs faster split, ripple trim, source In/Out, J/K/L playback, and page navigation habits.
avoid_when: The operator does not know the current keyboard mapping and shortcuts may trigger the wrong action.
A client project requires a locked keyboard preset or shared workstation mapping.
Speed would risk destructive edits without versioning or undo safety.

timeline_pattern.pattern: source_in_out -> jkl_review -> split_or_blade -> ripple_trim -> cut_silence -> option_drag_duplicate -> open_target_in_fusion -> select_left_or_right -> swap_clip_left_right -> record_voiceover_if_needed
timeline_pattern.custom_mapping_rule: Set split and ripple delete shortcuts only when the editor can confirm the current keyboard customization.
timeline_pattern.ripple_mapping_rule: Map frequent ripple-start/ripple-end actions to fast local keys only after confirming they will not conflict with shared keyboard presets.
timeline_pattern.playback_rule: Use J/K/L and source In/Out points to choose footage before dragging whole clips into the timeline.
timeline_pattern.selection_rule: Use select-left/select-right shortcuts to make space instead of manually lassoing clips.
timeline_pattern.swap_rule: Use clip swap shortcuts for reordering instead of dragging and rebuilding gaps.

motion.rule: Use shortcut speed to support clean timing; do not rush past motion/caption QC.

sound.rule: Resolve can record voiceover inside the app; still check levels and noise before using the recording. Waveform-based trimming is fast, but do not remove meaningful pauses.

captions.rule: Fast editing shortcuts should not skip caption collision checks after layout changes.

color.rule: Use viewer background color changes to inspect black edges or black elements against black backgrounds.

implementation.ffmpeg: Map repeated timeline operations to scripts or edit-decision transforms; keep dry-run previews before overwriting.
implementation.remotion: Represent repeated move/swap/select operations as data transforms on timeline arrays.
implementation.blender: Use shortcut-driven timeline and graph-editor workflows only after keyframes are named and organized.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use duplicate, split, ripple delete, and batch selection shortcuts where available; verify mappings.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use keyboard shortcuts for Add Edit, Ripple Delete, select clips forward/backward, duplicate, swap/reorder, and direct sequence navigation.

common_mistakes: Assuming another editor's shortcut map matches the local system.
Customizing shortcuts without documenting the mapping for the project or workstation.
Moving clips quickly without checking captions, SFX, or B-roll sync afterward.
Opening Fusion on the wrong visible layer because upper clips were selected or active.
Forgetting to inspect black-on-black edges or elements in the viewer.
qc: Are custom shortcut mappings documented for the project or workstation?
Were waveform-based trims reviewed so meaningful pauses were not removed?
After shortcut-based moves, are captions, SFX, and B-roll still synced?
Did the intended clip open in Fusion rather than an upper overlay?
Does the viewer background reveal any black edges or hidden black elements?
Was any in-app voiceover checked for level, noise, and timing?
